859.t: Eureka band members: trombones, bass, drummers
859.s: Gabriel and the interviewer sort out the Eureka band's trombonists, bassists, baritone player and its drummers.
859.ch: Parade bands, instruments and the Eureka band
859.q: And you played trombone for a while. Yeah. And then we had this fellow, big tall fellow played trombone. Warner. Oh, Albert Warner.

259.t: Dr. Ernest's band and Robert Taylor; Fuchs's big feet
259.s: After Duck, the band included Robert Taylor; Vincent names clarinet, drums and a bass drummer who died on parade, with an aside on a shoemaker named Fuchs.
259.q: With me? Yeah. He said, after you finished playing with me, who did you go with? When I finished playing? With me. Let me see. I remember Dr. Ernest. Dr. Ernest. He was playing out of Metro. He was playing with me. He was playing with me. He was playing with me. He was playing out of Metro. And…

860.t: Other New Orleans marching bands heard
860.s: Apart from Eureka he liked the Young Tuxedo band and recalls no others.
860.ch: Later band, return visits and marching band
860.q: tuxedo that i liked very much and i i don't think i heard i wouldn't be sure i don't think anybody like that any other band apart from them too

861.t: Street bands with Kid Howard and Kepard's broken horn
861.s: He was regular with Kid Howard and sometimes played for Abbey Williams; a story about borrowing Kepard's old horn.
861.q: I couldn't get to, Kepard had my horn and he left that old broken horn at his house and he went off and played somewhere and I had to go play, I had to have some kind of.

183.t: Favorite brass bands: Tuxedo, Olympia and Eureka, and John Casimir
183.s: Watts followed the Tuxedo brass band as a boy, first heard the Eureka in 1955, and John Casimir invited him to play with him.
183.q: Yeah, I guess so. I was so little, you know, as soon as I hear a band, you know, our kids used to be, you know, I'd run out there and get on the sidewalk and I'd be with that long second line. But I think that's the one I can remember more, you know, that I followed. The tuxedo. And then there used…

481.t: Chris Kelly, the Gibson band and brass bands under Jimmy Jackson
481.s: Bailey names Chris Kelly and Stutter as his main bands and discusses brass band work, Jimmy Jackson who managed the band, and picking up bass drum himself.
481.ch: Dave Bailey: brass bands and playing career
481.q: No, I don't have been playing with them, I only forgot to hold on. See, I just played with them, they just got the brass band, I played with the brass band.

282.t: Playing brass bands around New Orleans
282.s: He played street parades with the Tuxedo, George Williams and many unnamed pick-up brass bands.
282.ch: Tuba, brass bands and the road
282.q: And uh, then I started out with this making street parades and I had more work than I could handle. Which bands did you play with? I played with all of the bands around here. That's uh, I played with the Tuxedo. That's John Kazmi. And uh, George William. He had a good brass band at the time. Oh…

404.t: Night parades and the old brass bands
404.s: Night parades with brass bands such as Celestin's and Keppard's.

782.t: Brass band personnel and rhythm section problems
782.s: Further comments on trumpets, trombones, tuba and drum section, and on why the band does not play together.
782.ch: Brass bands, funerals and Swedish scene
782.q: It was two bass drums, two snare drums. Yeah. The day, the week before we only had one snare drum. Mm-hm. And the week before also Alan Jaffe was playing the tuba. Mm-hm. And then the rhythm session, they went out of the beat several times.

638.t: Algiers brass bands: Henry Allen, Atlantic and Pacific, Minetta
638.s: He recalls Algiers brass bands heard as a boy of eleven or twelve.
638.q: Well, I heard Allen band. I heard his band a lot of times. And they had another band over there. And they were all them fellas. I was about, during that time, and I was about around 11, 12 years old. But I know they had the Atlantic band. They had the Pacific band.

832.t: Playing snare drum in brass bands
832.s: Foster played snare drum in New Orleans brass bands with Amos Riley and Gus Metcalf and the Jefferson City Buds, and struggles to recall other players.
832.ch: Brass bands, country bands and Alamo
832.q: No, over there. I played over here. I mean here. Oh, yeah. I played brass band here with Amos. I played over Amos. I played with Gus Metcalf here. Brass bands. Jefferson Buds. You know? Yeah. Jefferson Buds.

825.t: Excelsior and Onward bands: instrumentation and marching in step
825.s: Ernie recalls the Excelsior and Onward bands, with their large instrumentation, constant rehearsal and every player stepping off together on the first beat, discipline he says is gone.
825.q: In other words, he kept all the music and everything. He was a good reader. Strictly most of the reader. He had the Eureka. Yeah, he enjoyed that Eureka then. He was really Carnage in the band then on Trinidad. No, Willie had died. He was out of there then. He was out of there. But I'm more sure…
